### `GridBreakpoint`

The grid's breakpoints, mobile first: `xs` is every width, `sm` from
576px, `md` from 768px, `lg` from 992px, `xl` from 1400px — the same
bands the layouts and the `.hide-*` / `.d-*-*` utilities use.

- `"xs"`
- `"sm"`
- `"md"`
- `"lg"`
- `"xl"`

### `GridColSpans`

A span per breakpoint, mobile first: a width applies from its
breakpoint upward until a larger one sets another. `{ sm: 6, lg: 3 }`
is full width on a phone, half from 576px and a quarter from 992px.

```ts
type GridColSpans = Partial
```

### `GridPhoneColumns`

Columns below 768px, where every `col-N` otherwise collapses to one.

- `"1"`
- `"2"`

### `GridGap`

The gutter between cells: `--space-2`, `--space-4` (default) or `--space-6`.

- `"sm"`
- `"md"`
- `"lg"`

### `GridProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Html[]` | yes |  |
| `phoneColumns` | `GridPhoneColumns` |  | Below 768px the grid is one column (every item full width) unless this says `"2"`: then items sit two-up — stat tiles, small cards — instead of stacking one tall tile per row. @default "1" |
| `gap` | `GridGap` |  | The gutter between cells. @default "md" |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `GridColProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `span` | `GridColSpan | GridColSpans` |  | How many of the 12 columns the cell spans. A number applies from 768px (`col-N`; below that every cell is full width, or two-up with `phoneColumns`). An object sets a span per breakpoint, mobile first (`col-xs-N` … `col-xl-N`): `{ xs: 6, md: 4, xl: 3 }`. |
| `content` | `Html` | yes |  |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

## Usage

Each example as the rAPId call and the HTML it renders — the markup a plain page writes by hand. Icons are inline SVG in the real output; they are shortened to `<svg …>…</svg>` here.

### Three stat tiles in a row

12 columns; every column collapses to full width below `md` — `phoneColumns: "2"` keeps tiles two-up on a phone.

```ts
Grid({
  phoneColumns: "2",
  items: [
    GridCol({ span: 4, content: Stat({ label: "Revenue", value: "$48,200" }) }),
    GridCol({ span: 4, content: Stat({ label: "Open", value: "12" }) }),
    GridCol({ span: 4, content: Stat({ label: "Overdue", value: "3", tone: "danger" }) }),
  ],
})
```

```html
<div class="grid grid--phone-2">
  <div class="col-4">
    <div class="stat">
      <span class="stat__label">Revenue</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">$48,200</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-4">
    <div class="stat">
      <span class="stat__label">Open</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">12</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-4">
    <div class="stat stat--danger">
      <span class="stat__label">Overdue</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">3</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### A span per breakpoint

An object span is mobile first: `{ xs: 6, md: 4, xl: 3 }` is two-up on a phone, three across from 768px and four from 1400px (`col-xs-6 col-md-4 col-xl-3`). A main column and an aside: `{ sm: 6, lg: 8 }` beside `{ sm: 6, lg: 4 }`.

```ts
Grid({
  gap: "sm",
  items: ["Revenue", "Open", "Overdue", "Paid"].map((label) =>
    GridCol({ span: { xs: 6, md: 4, xl: 3 }, content: Stat({ label, value: "12" }) })
  ),
})
```

```html
<div class="grid grid--gap-sm">
  <div class="col-xs-6 col-md-4 col-xl-3">
    <div class="stat">
      <span class="stat__label">Revenue</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">12</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-xs-6 col-md-4 col-xl-3">
    <div class="stat">
      <span class="stat__label">Open</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">12</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-xs-6 col-md-4 col-xl-3">
    <div class="stat">
      <span class="stat__label">Overdue</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">12</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-xs-6 col-md-4 col-xl-3">
    <div class="stat">
      <span class="stat__label">Paid</span>
      <span class="stat__row">
        <span class="stat__value">12</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
